column1: # /searched/ AS ROWS. Extracted 7 October 2026 from the page's own prose.
# *** THIS IS AN INDEX OVER THE PROSE, NOT A REPLACEMENT FOR IT. *** The page runs to 1,429 lines and
# thirty-three sections, several of which are themselves tables of many searches. Flattening that into
# five fields would have thrown away the reasoning, which on this page IS the asset - it is the archive's
# record of how it was wrong. So every row LINKS TO ITS SECTION and the sections stay exactly where they
# were. What the rows add is what the prose could never give: a thing a filter can reach and a gate can
# *** THE OUTCOME WORDS ARE THIS ARCHIVE'S OWN, which the kit insists on. *** The component's docstring
# says four archives grade their searches four different ways and that flattening them to a shared five
# "would be inventing a finding". Ours: found, nothing, mixed, blocked, answered, unresolved, abandoned.
# `nil` - the words that mean a search returned nothing - is just `nothing`, and that is the count the
# *** THREE SECTIONS ARE DELIBERATELY NOT ROWS: *** "Why a page of failures", "What is on this page" and
# "What the failures add up to". They are the page's argument about itself, not searches, and giving them
# an outcome would be a category error.
# `when` is coarse where the prose is coarse. A bare year means the section does not date itself more
# precisely, and guessing a day to fill a column is how a register starts lying.
# *** AND THE SAME BASE TRAP AS data/open-questions.tsv, IN A NEW SHAPE. *** `href` is passed
# through the kit's u(), so a BARE #anchor becomes /TheLerena/#anchor - a link to the home page that
# happens to carry a fragment no page there has. Thirty of them, every one caught by the anchor gate.
# The hrefs below are written /searched/#anchor so u() lands them on this page.
